rule_level_problems.problem: No system_priority_evaluation. The red box 'Treat as anaphylaxis' is the page's escalation, and the house standard turns the red box into a priority rule (gold: 'Urgent: Anaphylaxis' on (active_condition Anaphylaxis)). This file diagnoses probable anaphylaxis but never raises priority; it relies on the anaphylaxis page's rule, which may or may not be present in this ruleset.

rule_level_problems.problem: The page reaches 'pseudoallergic self-limiting rash likely' only after monitoring for at least 30 minutes with no other symptoms. The rule has no time condition, so it fires as soon as an isolated rash and the absences are recorded. (>= (onset (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Urticaria" "disorder"))) (time_ago 30 minutes)) would encode the window.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable pseudoallergic rash after vaccination
rule_level_problems.problem: (no Itching) excludes the common case of an itchy isolated urticarial rash. Such a patient fails this rule and, being single-system and not generalised or severe, also fails the anaphylaxis rule, so they end with no diagnosis. The page's 'without other symptoms' reads as other body systems; itch belongs to the same skin/mucosal group as the rash. Consider dropping the Itching and Nasal congestion exclusions, keeping the swelling ones (which the page names as return triggers).

The 'Do symptom/s improve quickly (minutes)?' gate is lost: faint/unwell findings count as a body system in any2 even when they resolve in minutes, so dizziness + nausea from a vasovagal episode yields probable anaphylaxis. Not fully representable; at minimum the remaining-questions record should carry it.

Hypotension is encoded as the recorded finding (clinical_finding Low blood pressure) rather than the routine BP measurement. The gold anaphylaxis page uses (< (measurement Systolic blood pressure mmHg) 90) / (< diastolic 60), which fires from vitals without a separate recording. The page gives no numeric threshold, so the finding form is defensible, but the two pages will disagree on what counts as hypotension.

rule_level_problems.rule: Check for adverse reaction after vaccination
rule_level_problems.problem: Swelling is encoded as Swelling + finding_site although SNOMED has precoordinated Lip swelling, Tongue swelling, Facial swelling, Swelling of hand and Swelling of eyelid (all finding). The finding_site form matches the gold anaphylaxis page, so this is consistent and should stay unless the whole ruleset changes; noted only so the choice is on record.

summary: The page's logic is captured well: all four symptom groups, the any2 body-system count, generalised urticaria and the serious single-system signs are encoded with existing SNOMED concepts and correct thresholds, and both 'likely' conclusions are probable rules. The most consequential gap is that nothing in the file escalates the patient the red box says to treat as anaphylaxis (no priority evaluation), followed by the pseudoallergic-rash rule firing without the page's 30-minute monitoring window and excluding itch, which leaves an itchy isolated rash with no diagnosis. The lost 'improve quickly' gate for faint symptoms is a known, largely unrepresentable over-trigger.
